title: Cloud, IoT & emerging tech
examples: What is the difference between public and private cloud?
Can you give an example of an IoT device I might find at home?
What kind of security risks are specific to IoT devices?

explain.say: Today we will explore cloud computing and the Internet of Things. These are very important modern technologies. We will look at how they work and what risks they carry.

items: Cloud Computing: Delivering services over the internet.
IoT: Connecting everyday physical objects to the internet.
Risks: Understanding the security challenges in these systems.

explain.say: First we look at cloud models. These models describe who owns and manages the cloud resources. There are three main types you should know.
A public cloud is like renting space on a large shared server. Many different companies can use the same physical infrastructure. Amazon Web Services is a common example of this.

draw.text: Public Cloud: Shared resources for many

explain.say: A private cloud means the computing resources are dedicated only to one group. This gives the organization maximum control over its data and security.

draw.text: Private Cloud: Dedicated to one group

explain.say: The hybrid cloud combines the best of both worlds for flexibility. You can keep sensitive data private while using public cloud power for less critical tasks.

draw.text: Hybrid Cloud: Combining public and private

explain.say: Now we look at IoT risks. Because these devices connect everywhere, they create many potential entry points for attackers. A simple smart thermostat is one such device.

faq.q: What is the main difference between public and private cloud?
faq.a: In a public cloud, resources are shared among many customers. A private cloud keeps resources dedicated only to your single organization.
asks: Does private cloud mean it's always better?

faq.q: Why is the hybrid cloud useful?
faq.a: It lets you use the public cloud's power when you need it, but keep your most sensitive data locked down in a private environment.
asks: Can I mix and match clouds?
What is the benefit of mixing cloud types?

faq.a: Many IoT devices have weak security built-in. They often lack strong passwords or regular updates, making them easy targets.
asks: How do I secure my smart home devices?

faq.q: Does cloud computing mean data is always safe?
faq.a: No, while providers use high security, data can still be at risk if the user sets up weak access controls or permissions.
asks: What is the biggest cloud risk?

faq.q: If I use a private cloud, am I completely immune to hacking?
faq.a: No, even private clouds require strong internal security management. The risk shifts from external sharing to internal management failure.
asks: What do I need to secure a private cloud?

facts: Public cloud services are useful for rapid scaling of resources.
A private cloud offers maximum control over data security and compliance.
IoT devices often connect via low-power wireless networks.
A major IoT risk is the lack of physical security on the device itself.

quiz.say: A company needs maximum control over its sensitive patient data, using resources only for itself. Which cloud model is best?
quiz.why: A private cloud dedicates resources solely to one organization, providing the highest level of control needed for sensitive data.

wrong.0: This is tempting because it is flexible, but the requirement here is for total, dedicated control.
wrong.1: This is tempting because it is fully controlled, but the question asks specifically about cloud models.
wrong.3: This is tempting because it is easy to set up, but sharing resources with others reduces control.

quiz.say: A farmer uses sensors to monitor soil moisture levels across many fields. This setup primarily relies on:
quiz.why: IoT involves connecting physical objects, like soil sensors, to the internet to collect and transmit data.

wrong.0: The farm does not necessarily need a private cloud; the connectivity is the key element here.
wrong.1: Encryption is a security measure applied to the data, not the core technology connecting the objects.
wrong.3: The cloud is where the data is stored, but the sensors themselves define the IoT aspect.

quiz.say: A student uses a service that keeps their general photos online but keeps their confidential exam notes on a local, dedicated server. This setup represents:
quiz.why: The combination of a public service (photos) and a private, dedicated resource (notes) defines a hybrid model.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the student is utilizing a cloud service for their photos.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the confidential notes are kept separately, not in the shared public space.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the general photos are stored using a publicly accessible service.
